<!-- The analysis of composition, beside the text that reports it, as in
     04.1_richness.qmd. It starts from what 03_methods.qmd prepares, n_perm
     included.
     A scientific name written by R code still goes in italics: put the
     asterisks around the inline code. check_species_text() reads the names
     you type; it cannot read the ones R writes. -->

```{r}
#| label: composition-model
#| cache: true
# n_perm permutations, set in 03_methods.qmd. They take a few seconds, once:
# the chunk is cached.
# Bray-Curtis dissimilarities between plots, on square-root abundances, so
# that the few very abundant species do not decide everything.
Y_sqrt <- sqrt(Y_counts)
d_bray <- vegdist(Y_sqrt, method = "bray")

# PERMANOVA: does the composition differ among habitats?
perm     <- adonis2(d_bray ~ habitat, permutations = n_perm, by = "terms")
tab_perm <- as.data.frame(perm)
r2_hab   <- tab_perm["habitat", "R2"]
f_hab    <- tab_perm["habitat", "F"]
pp_hab   <- tab_perm["habitat", "Pr(>F)"]

# PERMDISP: do the habitats differ in how variable their composition is?
disp   <- betadisper(d_bray, habitat)
pdisp  <- permutest(disp, permutations = n_perm)
f_disp <- pdisp$tab["Groups", "F"]
p_disp <- pdisp$tab["Groups", "Pr(>F)"]

# NMDS of the same dissimilarities.
nmds <- metaMDS(Y_sqrt, distance = "bray", k = 2, trymax = 50,
                autotransform = FALSE, trace = FALSE)

# The six most abundant species, named on the ordination.
top_sp <- species[order(colSums(Y_counts), decreasing = TRUE)[1:6]]
```

## Assemblage composition

The composition of the tree assemblages
`r if (pp_hab < 0.05) "differed" else "did not differ significantly"` among
habitats, which explained `r round(100 * r2_hab)`% of its variation
(PERMANOVA, *F* = `r round(f_hab, 2)`, *P* `r fmt_p(pp_hab)`;
@tbl-community), and the NMDS (stress `r round(nmds$stress, 2)`) ordered the
plots by habitat (@fig-nmds). The dispersions of the habitats
`r if (p_disp < 0.05) "also differed" else "did not differ"` (PERMDISP,
*F* = `r round(f_disp, 2)`, *P* `r fmt_p(p_disp)`), so the difference among
habitats `r if (p_disp < 0.05) "may in part be one of heterogeneity rather than of mean composition" else "is one of mean composition, not only of heterogeneity"`.
The most abundant species was
*`r sp_italic(top_sp[1])`*`r sp_roman(top_sp[1])`, with
`r format(sum(Y_counts[, top_sp[1]]), big.mark = ",")` trees.

The `r n_top` most abundant species are listed in @stbl-species, and the
abundance of every species, ranked, is in @sfig-rankabund.
